3-5.def: facts or details that support an idea
3-5.ex: The footprints are evidence that an animal passed by.
3-5.clip: Maya says the pond is shrinking. Her evidence is a muddy ring that is two feet wide around the edge.
3-5.clipEs: Maya dice que el estanque se está encogiendo. Su evidencia es un anillo de lodo de dos pies de ancho alrededor del borde.
3-5.q: What is Maya's evidence?
3-5.a: A muddy ring around the pond

3-5.def: to figure out something using clues and what you already know
3-5.ex: I infer that she is cold because she is shivering.
3-5.clip: Raj sees wet boots by the door and an open umbrella. He infers that it rained while he was inside.
3-5.clipEs: Raj ve botas mojadas junto a la puerta y un paraguas abierto. Infiere que llovió mientras él estaba adentro.
3-5.q: What clues help Raj infer it rained?
3-5.a: Wet boots and an open umbrella

3-5.def: to tell the most important parts in a few words
3-5.ex: Please summarize the story in two sentences.
3-5.clip: After reading about volcanoes, Lena summarizes the text. She names how they form and why they erupt.
3-5.clipEs: Después de leer sobre los volcanes, Lena resume el texto. Dice cómo se forman y por qué hacen erupción.
3-5.q: What does Lena include in her summary?

3-5.def: to explain how two things are different
3-5.ex: We contrast a frog and a toad.
3-5.clip: The students contrast frogs and toads. Frogs have smooth skin, but toads have bumpy skin.
3-5.clipEs: Los estudiantes contrastan ranas y sapos. Las ranas tienen piel lisa, pero los sapos tienen piel con bultos.
3-5.q: Which animal has bumpy skin?

3-5.def: to change in a way that helps you live in a place
3-5.ex: Camels adapt to the desert.
3-5.clip: Polar bears adapt to the cold. They have thick fur and a layer of fat to stay warm.
3-5.clipEs: Los osos polares se adaptan al frío. Tienen pelaje grueso y una capa de grasa para mantenerse calientes.
3-5.q: How do polar bears stay warm?

3-5.def: everything around a living thing, like air, water, and land
3-5.ex: A clean environment helps fish live.
3-5.clip: The class cleans the stream. A cleaner environment gives the fish clear water to live in.
3-5.clipEs: La clase limpia el arroyo. Un ambiente más limpio da a los peces agua clara para vivir.
3-5.q: What does the cleaner stream give the fish?

3-5.def: something people or animals can use, like water or wood
3-5.ex: Water is a natural resource.
3-5.clip: The town builds a well to share a resource. Everyone uses the clean water carefully.
3-5.clipEs: El pueblo construye un pozo para compartir un recurso. Todos usan el agua limpia con cuidado.
3-5.q: What resource does the town share?

3-5.def: living and nonliving things that depend on each other in a place
3-5.ex: A pond is an ecosystem.
3-5.clip: In a forest ecosystem, trees give shade, insects eat leaves, and birds eat insects.
3-5.clipEs: En un ecosistema de bosque, los árboles dan sombra, los insectos comen hojas y las aves comen insectos.
3-5.q: What do birds eat in this ecosystem?

3-5.def: an animal that hunts other animals for food
3-5.ex: An owl is a predator of mice.
3-5.clip: The hawk is a predator. It circles above the field and looks for a mouse.
3-5.clipEs: El halcón es un depredador. Da vueltas sobre el campo y busca un ratón.
3-5.q: What does the hawk look for?

3-5.def: a test that helps you answer a question
3-5.ex: We do an experiment with magnets.
3-5.clip: Ines runs an experiment. She tests which objects a magnet picks up and writes each result.
3-5.clipEs: Inés hace un experimento. Prueba qué objetos atrae un imán y anota cada resultado.
3-5.q: What does Ines write down?

3-5.def: to watch carefully and notice details
3-5.ex: Observe the beetle for two minutes.
3-5.clip: The class observes a snail for ten minutes. They notice that it leaves a shiny trail.
3-5.clipEs: La clase observa un caracol durante diez minutos. Notan que deja un rastro brillante.
3-5.q: What do they notice about the snail?

3-5.def: to decide something after thinking about facts
3-5.ex: We conclude that plants need light.
3-5.clip: After three weeks, the group concludes that the plant in the sun grew taller than the plant in the closet.
3-5.clipEs: Después de tres semanas, el grupo concluye que la planta al sol creció más que la planta del armario.
3-5.q: Which plant grew taller?

3-5.def: the way parts are put together
3-5.ex: The bridge has a strong structure.
3-5.clip: Triangles make the bridge structure strong. The builders add more triangles near the middle.
3-5.clipEs: Los triángulos hacen fuerte la estructura del puente. Los constructores añaden más triángulos cerca del centro.
3-5.q: Where do the builders add triangles?

3-5.def: the reason something happens
3-5.ex: The cause of the flood was heavy rain.
3-5.clip: Heavy rain was the cause of the flooded street. The drains were full of leaves.
3-5.clipEs: La lluvia fuerte fue la causa de la calle inundada. Los desagües estaban llenos de hojas.
3-5.q: What was the cause of the flooded street?

3-5.def: what happens because of something else
3-5.ex: Sleepiness is an effect of staying up late.
3-5.clip: One effect of the drought is dry soil. The farmers must water the crops more often.
3-5.clipEs: Un efecto de la sequía es la tierra seca. Los agricultores deben regar los cultivos con más frecuencia.
3-5.q: What is one effect of the drought?

3-5.def: an answer to a problem
3-5.ex: We found a solution to the problem.
3-5.clip: The school has a trash problem. Students suggest a solution: add recycling bins near the door.
3-5.clipEs: La escuela tiene un problema de basura. Los estudiantes sugieren una solución: poner contenedores de reciclaje cerca de la puerta.
3-5.q: What is the students' solution?

3-5.def: something difficult that needs a solution
3-5.ex: The character has a big problem.
3-5.clip: In the story, Nico has a problem. He loses the key to the clubhouse.
3-5.clipEs: En el cuento, Nico tiene un problema. Pierde la llave de la casita club.
3-5.q: What is Nico's problem?

3-5.def: a person or animal in a story
3-5.ex: The main character is a girl named Tala.
3-5.clip: The main character, Tala, feels nervous on her first day. Her new teacher greets her with a smile.
3-5.clipEs: La personaje principal, Tala, se siente nerviosa en su primer día. Su nueva maestra la saluda con una sonrisa.
3-5.q: How does Tala feel?

3-5.def: where and when a story takes place
3-5.ex: The setting is a farm in summer.
3-5.clip: The story's setting is a harbor town at night. Fog covers the boats and lamps.
3-5.clipEs: El escenario del cuento es un pueblo de puerto de noche. La niebla cubre los botes y las lámparas.
3-5.q: When does the story take place?

3-5.def: the voice that tells a story
3-5.ex: The narrator tells us what happens.
3-5.clip: The narrator tells the story from the dog's point of view. We learn what the dog smells and hears.
3-5.clipEs: El narrador cuenta la historia desde el punto de vista del perro. Sabemos lo que el perro huele y oye.
3-5.q: Whose point of view does the narrator use?

3-5.def: the way a person sees or thinks about something
3-5.ex: Each character has a different perspective.
3-5.clip: Eli thinks the rain ruins the picnic, but his sister's perspective is different. She loves jumping in puddles.
3-5.clipEs: Eli piensa que la lluvia arruina el picnic, pero la perspectiva de su hermana es distinta. A ella le encanta saltar en los charcos.
3-5.q: What does Eli's sister love?

3-5.def: what you think or feel about something
3-5.ex: In my opinion, summer is the best season.
3-5.clip: Hana's opinion is that the park needs more trees. She gives two reasons to support it.
3-5.clipEs: La opinión de Hana es que el parque necesita más árboles. Da dos razones para apoyarla.
3-5.q: How many reasons does Hana give?

3-5.def: to help someone believe or agree with you
3-5.ex: I want to convince you to read this book.
3-5.clip: Sam wants to convince his parents to adopt a dog. He shows them a list of how he will help.
3-5.clipEs: Sam quiere convencer a sus padres de adoptar un perro. Les muestra una lista de cómo ayudará.
3-5.q: How does Sam try to convince them?

3-5.def: a large area with something in common
3-5.ex: The desert region is hot and dry.
3-5.clip: The northern region of the country gets cold winters. The southern region stays warm all year.
3-5.clipEs: La región norte del país tiene inviernos fríos. La región sur se mantiene cálida todo el año.
3-5.q: Which region stays warm all year?

3-5.def: the usual weather in a place over many years
3-5.ex: The climate here is warm and wet.
3-5.clip: The climate in the rainforest is warm and wet all year. Plants there grow very tall.
3-5.clipEs: El clima de la selva tropical es cálido y húmedo todo el año. Las plantas allí crecen muy altas.
3-5.q: How is the rainforest climate?

3-5.def: to travel to another place for a season
3-5.ex: Geese migrate south in the fall.
3-5.clip: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles. They fly south before winter.
3-5.clipEs: Las mariposas monarca migran miles de millas. Vuelan al sur antes del invierno.
3-5.q: When do the butterflies fly south?

3-5.def: the slow wearing away of rock or soil by water or wind
3-5.ex: Rain caused erosion on the hill.
3-5.clip: Erosion is wearing away the riverbank. Each spring, the fast water carries more soil downstream.
3-5.clipEs: La erosión está desgastando la orilla del río. Cada primavera, el agua rápida arrastra más tierra río abajo.
3-5.q: What carries the soil downstream?

3-5.def: a number that names equal parts of a whole
3-5.ex: One half is a fraction.
3-5.clip: Mia cuts a pizza into eight equal slices. She eats three slices, which is the fraction three-eighths.
3-5.clipEs: Mia corta una pizza en ocho rebanadas iguales. Come tres rebanadas, que es la fracción tres octavos.
3-5.q: How many slices does Mia eat?

3-5.def: to make a careful guess about a number or amount
3-5.ex: I estimate it will take ten minutes.
3-5.clip: Before counting, Leo estimates how many beans are in the jar. He says about fifty.
3-5.clipEs: Antes de contar, Leo estima cuántos frijoles hay en el frasco. Dice que unos cincuenta.
3-5.q: What does Leo do before counting?

3-5.def: having the same amount or value
3-5.ex: Two halves are equal parts.
3-5.clip: The twins split the cookie into equal parts. Each twin gets the same amount.
3-5.clipEs: Los gemelos dividen la galleta en partes iguales. Cada gemelo recibe la misma cantidad.
3-5.q: How do the twins split the cookie?

3-5.def: facts and numbers collected to learn about something
3-5.ex: The data show that most students walk.
3-5.clip: Students collect data on how they get to school. The data show that twelve walk and eight ride the bus.
3-5.clipEs: Los estudiantes recopilan datos sobre cómo llegan a la escuela. Los datos muestran que doce caminan y ocho van en autobús.
3-5.q: How many students ride the bus?

3-5.def: a drawing that shows numbers or data
3-5.ex: The graph shows how many books we read.
3-5.clip: The bar graph shows favorite fruits. The tallest bar is for strawberries.
3-5.clipEs: La gráfica de barras muestra las frutas favoritas. La barra más alta es la de fresas.
3-5.q: Which fruit has the tallest bar?

3-5.def: letters added to the start of a word that change its meaning
3-5.ex: Un is a prefix in the word unhappy.
3-5.clip: The prefix re means again. If you reread a book, you read it again.
3-5.clipEs: El prefijo re significa de nuevo. Si relees un libro, lo lees otra vez.
3-5.q: What does the prefix re mean?

3-5.def: the words you know and use
3-5.ex: I learn new vocabulary every week.
3-5.clip: Dana keeps a notebook for new vocabulary. She writes each word with a picture and a sentence.
3-5.clipEs: Dana guarda un cuaderno para el vocabulario nuevo. Escribe cada palabra con un dibujo y una oración.
3-5.q: What does Dana write with each word?

3-5.def: a person who helps without being paid
3-5.ex: My aunt is a volunteer at the shelter.
3-5.clip: Every Saturday, a volunteer reads to children at the library. Nobody pays her, but she loves to help.
3-5.clipEs: Todos los sábados, una voluntaria lee a los niños en la biblioteca. Nadie le paga, pero le encanta ayudar.
3-5.q: Does the volunteer get paid?

3-5.def: something a family or group does for many years
3-5.ex: Baking bread on Sundays is our tradition.
3-5.clip: Every winter, Tomas's family makes tamales together. It is a tradition from his great-grandmother.
3-5.clipEs: Cada invierno, la familia de Tomás hace tamales juntos. Es una tradición de su bisabuela.
3-5.q: When does the family make tamales?

3-5.def: to mark a special day or event with others
3-5.ex: Families celebrate in many ways.
3-5.clip: Diwali is a festival of lights. Families celebrate with lamps, sweets, and time together.
3-5.clipEs: Diwali es una fiesta de las luces. Las familias celebran con lámparas, dulces y tiempo juntos.
3-5.q: How do families celebrate Diwali?
3-5.a: With lamps, sweets, and time together

3-5.def: a talk where you ask someone questions to learn about them
3-5.ex: We did an interview with a firefighter.
3-5.clip: Priya prepares five questions for an interview with the baker. She writes the answers in her notebook.
3-5.clipEs: Priya prepara cinco preguntas para una entrevista con el panadero. Anota las respuestas en su cuaderno.
3-5.q: How many questions does Priya prepare?

3-5.def: a set of questions asked to many people to collect information
3-5.ex: Our class made a survey about pets.
3-5.clip: The class takes a survey about favorite lunches. Pizza gets the most votes.
3-5.clipEs: La clase hace una encuesta sobre almuerzos favoritos. La pizza recibe más votos.
3-5.q: What gets the most votes?

3-5.def: to turn around a center point
3-5.ex: Earth rotates once each day.
3-5.clip: Earth rotates once a day. When your side faces away from the sun, it is night.
3-5.clipEs: La Tierra gira una vez al día. Cuando tu lado mira lejos del sol, es de noche.
3-5.q: When is it night?
3-5.a: When your side faces away from the sun

3-5.def: to soak up or take in
3-5.ex: A sponge can absorb water.
3-5.clip: Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun. A white shirt reflects more light.
3-5.clipEs: La ropa oscura absorbe más calor del sol. Una camiseta blanca refleja más luz.
3-5.q: Which clothes absorb more heat?

3-5.def: to bounce light or sound back
3-5.ex: A mirror will reflect light.
3-5.clip: A mirror reflects the flashlight beam onto the wall. Mei moves the mirror and the spot of light moves too.
3-5.clipEs: Un espejo refleja el rayo de la linterna sobre la pared. Mei mueve el espejo y la mancha de luz también se mueve.
3-5.q: What happens when Mei moves the mirror?

3-5.def: to move back and forth very fast
3-5.ex: A guitar string vibrates when you pluck it.
3-5.clip: When Omar plucks the string, it vibrates and makes a sound. He touches it and the sound stops.
3-5.clipEs: Cuando Omar toca la cuerda, vibra y hace un sonido. La toca con el dedo y el sonido se detiene.
3-5.q: What happens when Omar touches the string?

3-5.def: to use carefully so it lasts
3-5.ex: We conserve water when we brush our teeth.
3-5.clip: The town asks everyone to conserve water during the dry summer. Families take shorter showers.
3-5.clipEs: El pueblo pide a todos conservar agua durante el verano seco. Las familias se bañan más rápido.
3-5.q: What do families do to conserve water?

3-5.def: to make old things into new things
3-5.ex: We recycle paper and cans.
3-5.clip: The factory will recycle old bottles into new ones. First, workers wash and melt the glass.
3-5.clipEs: La fábrica reciclará botellas viejas para hacer botellas nuevas. Primero, los trabajadores lavan y derriten el vidrio.
3-5.q: What do workers do first?

3-5.def: to make something with care and skill
3-5.ex: The author crafts her sentences carefully.
3-5.clip: The poet crafts each line with care. She reads it aloud and changes words until it sounds right.
3-5.clipEs: La poeta elabora cada verso con cuidado. Lo lee en voz alta y cambia palabras hasta que suena bien.
3-5.q: How does the poet check each line?

3-5.def: something difficult that tests your skills
3-5.ex: The puzzle is a good challenge.
3-5.clip: The class takes on a challenge: build the tallest tower from paper. They work as a team for twenty minutes.
3-5.clipEs: La clase acepta un desafío: construir la torre más alta con papel. Trabajan en equipo veinte minutos.
3-5.q: What are they building?

3-5.def: to change writing to make it clearer or better
3-5.ex: I revise my paragraph after my partner reads it.
3-5.clip: Kai revises his story after a partner reads it. He adds a sentence to show how the dog feels.
3-5.clipEs: Kai revisa su cuento después de que un compañero lo lee. Añade una oración para mostrar cómo se siente el perro.
3-5.q: What does Kai add?
3-5.a: A sentence about the dog's feelings

3-5.def: a small piece of information that adds to the main idea
3-5.ex: A good detail helps readers picture the scene.
3-5.clip: The main idea is that bees help gardens. One detail is that bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
3-5.clipEs: La idea principal es que las abejas ayudan a los jardines. Un detalle es que las abejas llevan polen de flor en flor.
3-5.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower?

3-5.def: a book, person, or place that gives you information
3-5.ex: The encyclopedia is a good source.
3-5.clip: For her report, Rosa uses two sources: a library book and an interview with a park ranger.
3-5.clipEs: Para su informe, Rosa usa dos fuentes: un libro de la biblioteca y una entrevista con un guardaparques.
3-5.q: What are Rosa's sources?

3-5.def: a feature of a living thing, like eye color or being kind
3-5.ex: Curly hair is a trait that can be inherited.
3-5.clip: Some puppies inherit a trait from their parents, like brown fur. Others have fur like the other parent.
3-5.clipEs: Algunos cachorros heredan un rasgo de sus padres, como el pelaje café. Otros tienen pelaje como el otro padre.
3-5.q: What trait do some puppies inherit?

3-5.def: a push or pull on an object
3-5.ex: Gravity is a force that pulls things down.
3-5.clip: When Ana pushes the cart, the force makes it roll. When she pulls harder, it rolls faster.
3-5.clipEs: Cuando Ana empuja el carrito, la fuerza lo hace rodar. Cuando jala más fuerte, rueda más rápido.
3-5.q: What happens when Ana pulls harder?

3-5.def: a force that slows things down when they rub together
3-5.ex: Friction slows the sled on the grass.
3-5.clip: A toy car goes farther on a smooth floor than on a rug. The rug has more friction, so the car slows down.
3-5.clipEs: Un carrito de juguete llega más lejos en un piso liso que en una alfombra. La alfombra tiene más fricción, así que el carrito se frena.
3-5.q: Why does the car slow down on the rug?

3-5.def: a path that electricity can flow around
3-5.ex: A bulb lights when the circuit is complete.
3-5.clip: The bulb stays dark because the circuit has a gap. When Jo connects the last wire, the bulb lights up.
3-5.clipEs: La bombilla sigue apagada porque el circuito tiene un hueco. Cuando Jo conecta el último cable, la bombilla se enciende.
3-5.q: Why is the bulb dark at first?

3-5.def: two or more things put together that can still be separated
3-5.ex: Trail mix is a mixture of nuts and raisins.
3-5.clip: The class pours sand and salt together to make a mixture. Then they add water to separate the salt.
3-5.clipEs: La clase mezcla arena y sal para hacer una mezcla. Luego agregan agua para separar la sal.
3-5.q: What do they add to separate the salt?

3-5.def: the distance around the outside of a shape
3-5.ex: The perimeter of the garden is twenty feet.
3-5.clip: The garden is a rectangle with sides of six feet and four feet. Eli adds all four sides to find the perimeter.
3-5.clipEs: El jardín es un rectángulo con lados de seis pies y cuatro pies. Eli suma los cuatro lados para hallar el perímetro.
3-5.q: What does Eli do to find the perimeter?

3-5.def: when one half of a shape matches the other half
3-5.ex: A butterfly has symmetry.
3-5.clip: Lina folds the paper heart in half. Both halves match, so the heart has symmetry.
3-5.clipEs: Lina dobla en dos el corazón de papel. Las dos mitades coinciden, así que el corazón tiene simetría.
3-5.q: How does Lina check for symmetry?

3-5.def: a number written with a dot, like 2.5
3-5.ex: A decimal can show part of a whole.
3-5.clip: The runner finishes in 9.8 seconds. The decimal point shows that part of a second counts, too.
3-5.clipEs: El corredor termina en 9,8 segundos. El punto decimal muestra que también cuenta una parte del segundo.
3-5.q: What does the decimal point show?

3-5.def: to carry pollen so plants can make seeds
3-5.ex: Bees pollinate flowers.
3-5.clip: Bees pollinate the apple blossoms. Without them, the tree would grow fewer apples.
3-5.clipEs: Las abejas polinizan las flores del manzano. Sin ellas, el árbol daría menos manzanas.
3-5.q: What would happen without the bees?

3-5.def: to get a trait from a parent
3-5.ex: Kittens inherit traits from their parents.
3-5.clip: Kittens inherit their fur color from their parents. A gray mother and a gray father often have gray kittens.
3-5.clipEs: Los gatitos heredan el color del pelaje de sus padres. Una madre gris y un padre gris suelen tener gatitos grises.
3-5.q: What do kittens inherit?

6-8.def: to study something closely by looking at its parts
6-8.ex: We analyze the data in the table.
6-8.clip: The students analyze their plant data. They notice that the plants with more light grew taller each week.
6-8.clipEs: Los estudiantes analizan los datos de sus plantas. Notan que las plantas con más luz crecieron más cada semana.
6-8.q: What do the students notice?
6-8.a: Plants with more light grew taller
x: All the plants grew the same

6-8.def: to judge how good or useful something is
6-8.ex: Evaluate the source before you use it.
6-8.clip: Before using a website, Nadia evaluates it. She checks who wrote it, when it was written, and whether it lists sources.
6-8.clipEs: Antes de usar un sitio web, Nadia lo evalúa. Revisa quién lo escribió, cuándo y si cita fuentes.
6-8.q: What does Nadia check first?

6-8.def: a statement that something is true
6-8.ex: The author makes a claim and supports it with evidence.
6-8.clip: The writer's claim is that school should start later. She supports it with a study about teenagers and sleep.
6-8.clipEs: La afirmación de la autora es que la escuela debería empezar más tarde. La apoya con un estudio sobre adolescentes y sueño.
6-8.q: How does the writer support her claim?

6-8.def: to explain what something means
6-8.ex: We interpret the graph to see the trend.
6-8.clip: Marcus interprets the line graph. The line rises each month, so he explains that sales are growing.
6-8.clipEs: Marcus interpreta la gráfica de líneas. La línea sube cada mes, así que explica que las ventas están creciendo.
6-8.q: What does the rising line show?

6-8.def: important enough to notice; large enough to matter
6-8.ex: The difference between the two groups is significant.
6-8.clip: The temperature rose by one degree, which is small. But a rise of ten degrees would be significant for the ocean.
6-8.clipEs: La temperatura subió un grado, lo cual es poco. Pero un aumento de diez grados sería significativo para el océano.
6-8.q: Which change would be significant?

6-8.def: one thing that helps cause a result
6-8.ex: Sunlight is a factor in how fast plants grow.
6-8.clip: Several factors affect how fast ice melts, such as temperature and wind. Amir changes only one factor in his test.
6-8.clipEs: Varios factores afectan qué tan rápido se derrite el hielo, como la temperatura y el viento. Amir cambia solo un factor en su prueba.
6-8.q: How many factors does Amir change?

6-8.def: a result of an action or event
6-8.ex: Pollution has serious consequences for rivers.
6-8.clip: One consequence of cutting the trees was more erosion. Rain washed the loose soil into the stream.
6-8.clipEs: Una consecuencia de talar los árboles fue más erosión. La lluvia arrastró la tierra suelta al arroyo.
6-8.q: What was one consequence of cutting the trees?

6-8.def: able to be trusted to be correct or to work well
6-8.ex: A reliable source gives accurate information.
6-8.clip: A museum website is a reliable source because experts check its facts. A random post with no author is less reliable.
6-8.clipEs: El sitio web de un museo es una fuente confiable porque expertos revisan sus datos. Una publicación al azar sin autor es menos confiable.
6-8.q: Why is the museum website reliable?

6-8.def: a strong leaning toward one side that is not fair
6-8.ex: The article shows bias against the new rule.
6-8.clip: The review is full of bias. The writer only mentions the bad parts of the game and never the good parts.
6-8.clipEs: La reseña está llena de sesgo. El escritor solo menciona las partes malas del juego y nunca las buenas.
6-8.q: What shows the writer's bias?
6-8.a: Only the bad parts are mentioned

6-8.def: to communicate an idea or feeling
6-8.ex: The poem conveys a feeling of loneliness.
6-8.clip: The photographer conveys joy by showing children laughing in the rain. The bright colors add to the feeling.
6-8.clipEs: El fotógrafo transmite alegría al mostrar a niños riendo bajo la lluvia. Los colores brillantes aumentan el sentimiento.
6-8.q: What feeling does the photograph convey?

6-8.def: to suggest something without saying it directly
6-8.ex: The narrator implies that the house is empty.
6-8.clip: The author implies that Lucas is nervous. She writes that his hands shake and he keeps checking the clock.
6-8.clipEs: La autora insinúa que Lucas está nervioso. Escribe que le tiemblan las manos y que mira el reloj una y otra vez.
6-8.q: What does the author imply about Lucas?

6-8.def: to combine ideas from different sources into one understanding
6-8.ex: Synthesize what you learned from both articles.
6-8.clip: Ivy reads three articles about wind energy. She synthesizes them into one explanation that uses facts from each source.
6-8.clipEs: Ivy lee tres artículos sobre energía eólica. Los sintetiza en una explicación que usa datos de cada fuente.
6-8.q: What does Ivy combine?

6-8.def: to give good reasons for a choice or answer
6-8.ex: Justify your answer with evidence from the text.
6-8.clip: Dev justifies his choice. He points to a sentence in the passage and explains why it supports his answer.
6-8.clipEs: Dev justifica su elección. Señala una oración del texto y explica por qué apoya su respuesta.
6-8.q: How does Dev justify his choice?
6-8.a: He points to a sentence in the text

6-8.def: a general direction that data or events are moving
6-8.ex: The trend shows more students using bikes.
6-8.clip: The graph shows an upward trend. Every year, more students choose to ride bikes to school.
6-8.clipEs: La gráfica muestra una tendencia al alza. Cada año, más estudiantes eligen ir en bicicleta a la escuela.
6-8.q: What does the upward trend show?
6-8.a: More students ride bikes each year

6-8.def: something in an experiment that can change
6-8.ex: The variable we change is the amount of water.
6-8.clip: In the experiment, the amount of light is the variable. All the other conditions, like soil and water, stay the same.
6-8.clipEs: En el experimento, la cantidad de luz es la variable. Todas las demás condiciones, como la tierra y el agua, se mantienen iguales.
6-8.q: What is the variable in the experiment?

6-8.def: an idea you can test that explains something
6-8.ex: Our hypothesis is that warm water dissolves sugar faster.
6-8.clip: Before the test, Lila writes a hypothesis: if the water is warmer, the sugar will dissolve faster. Then she times each cup.
6-8.clipEs: Antes de la prueba, Lila escribe una hipótesis: si el agua está más tibia, el azúcar se disolverá más rápido. Luego cronometra cada vaso.
6-8.q: What does Lila's hypothesis say?

6-8.def: a decision or final idea based on evidence
6-8.ex: Our conclusion is supported by the data.
6-8.clip: Her conclusion matches the results: the warm water dissolved the sugar in twenty seconds, but the cold water needed a minute.
6-8.clipEs: Su conclusión coincide con los resultados: el agua tibia disolvió el azúcar en veinte segundos, pero el agua fría necesitó un minuto.
6-8.q: How long did the warm water take?

6-8.def: to show that an idea is wrong using evidence
6-8.ex: The new data refute the old theory.
6-8.clip: Mia refutes the claim that plants need no light. She shows photos of the plants that died in the dark closet.
6-8.clipEs: Mia refuta la afirmación de que las plantas no necesitan luz. Muestra fotos de las plantas que murieron en el armario oscuro.
6-8.q: What does Mia show to refute the claim?
6-8.a: Photos of plants that died in the dark
x: A list of her favorite plants

6-8.def: used to show a contrast with what was just said
6-8.ex: The test was hard; however, I passed.
6-8.clip: Tara loves soccer. However, she also wants to try the school band, so she has to choose a schedule.
6-8.clipEs: A Tara le encanta el fútbol. Sin embargo, también quiere probar la banda escolar, así que debe elegir un horario.
6-8.q: What else does Tara want to try?

6-8.def: used to show a result of what was just said
6-8.ex: It was raining; therefore, we stayed home.
6-8.clip: The river is rising quickly. Therefore, the town asks families near the bank to move to higher ground.
6-8.clipEs: El río está subiendo rápidamente. Por lo tanto, el pueblo pide a las familias cerca de la orilla que se muden a un terreno más alto.
6-8.q: What does the town ask families to do?

6-8.def: used to introduce an idea that contrasts with another
6-8.ex: Although it was late, we kept working.
6-8.clip: Although the experiment failed, the team learned something useful. They knew which wire had been loose.
6-8.clipEs: Aunque el experimento falló, el equipo aprendió algo útil. Supieron cuál cable estaba flojo.
6-8.q: What did the team learn?

6-8.def: used to compare two things that are different
6-8.ex: Frogs live near water, whereas toads often live on dry land.
6-8.clip: Cats hunt alone, whereas wolves hunt in groups. Each way helps the animals find food.
6-8.clipEs: Los gatos cazan solos, mientras que los lobos cazan en grupos. Cada manera ayuda a los animales a encontrar comida.
6-8.q: How do wolves hunt?

6-8.def: used to add another important point
6-8.ex: The park is safe; furthermore, it is free.
6-8.clip: The bike lane reduces traffic. Furthermore, it lowers pollution and makes the street quieter.
6-8.clipEs: El carril bici reduce el tráfico. Además, baja la contaminación y hace la calle más tranquila.
6-8.q: What else does the bike lane do?

6-8.def: used to show something is true despite what was just said
6-8.ex: It was hard; nevertheless, she finished.
6-8.clip: The path was steep and muddy. Nevertheless, the hikers kept going, and they reached the top by noon.
6-8.clipEs: El sendero era empinado y lleno de lodo. Sin embargo, los excursionistas siguieron y llegaron a la cima al mediodía.
6-8.q: When did the hikers reach the top?

6-8.def: basic systems a community needs, like roads, pipes, and power lines
6-8.ex: The city is repairing its infrastructure.
6-8.clip: The storm damaged the town's infrastructure. Roads flooded, and power lines fell, so crews worked day and night.
6-8.clipEs: La tormenta dañó la infraestructura del pueblo. Las calles se inundaron y cayeron cables eléctricos, así que los equipos trabajaron día y noche.
6-8.q: What damaged the infrastructure?

6-8.def: able to continue without using up resources or harming the environment
6-8.ex: Solar energy is sustainable.
6-8.clip: The farm uses sustainable methods. It collects rainwater and plants different crops each year to keep the soil healthy.
6-8.clipEs: La granja usa métodos sostenibles. Recoge agua de lluvia y cambia de cultivos cada año para mantener sana la tierra.
6-8.q: How does the farm keep its soil healthy?
6-8.a: It plants different crops each year

6-8.def: a member of a country or community
6-8.ex: Every citizen can help improve the town.
6-8.clip: A citizen can write to the mayor about a problem. Rosa wrote a letter asking for a crosswalk near the school.
6-8.clipEs: Un ciudadano puede escribirle al alcalde sobre un problema. Rosa escribió una carta pidiendo un cruce peatonal cerca de la escuela.
6-8.q: What did Rosa ask for?

6-8.def: a person who moves to a new country to live
6-8.ex: My grandmother is an immigrant.
6-8.clip: Many immigrants bring foods and music from their home countries. They share these traditions in their new communities.
6-8.clipEs: Muchos inmigrantes traen comidas y música de sus países de origen. Comparten estas tradiciones en sus nuevas comunidades.
6-8.q: What do immigrants share?

6-8.def: the beliefs, customs, food, and art of a group of people
6-8.ex: Food is an important part of culture.
6-8.clip: Culture includes language, food, music, and holidays. At the school fair, each family shares a part of their culture.
6-8.clipEs: La cultura incluye el idioma, la comida, la música y las fiestas. En la feria escolar, cada familia comparte una parte de su cultura.
6-8.q: Where do families share their culture?

6-8.def: a system where people choose their leaders by voting
6-8.ex: In a democracy, citizens vote for leaders.
6-8.clip: In a democracy, the people vote for their leaders. The class practices by voting for a class president.
6-8.clipEs: En una democracia, la gente vota por sus líderes. La clase practica votando por un presidente de la clase.
6-8.q: How does the class practice democracy?
6-8.a: They vote for a class president

6-8.def: the movement of animals or people from one place to another
6-8.ex: The migration of whales takes months.
6-8.clip: The migration of gray whales covers about ten thousand miles. They swim from cold feeding waters to warm waters to have babies.
6-8.clipEs: La migración de las ballenas grises cubre unas diez mil millas. Nadan de aguas frías donde comen a aguas cálidas para tener sus crías.
6-8.q: Why do the whales swim to warm waters?

6-8.def: the way plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food
6-8.ex: Photosynthesis happens in the leaves.
6-8.clip: During photosynthesis, a plant uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar. It also releases oxygen into the air.
6-8.clipEs: Durante la fotosíntesis, una planta usa luz solar, agua y dióxido de carbono para producir azúcar. También libera oxígeno al aire.
6-8.q: What does the plant release?

6-8.def: the ability to do work or make things move or change
6-8.ex: The sun gives Earth energy.
6-8.clip: A battery stores energy. When Jo connects it to the motor, the energy makes the toy car move.
6-8.clipEs: Una pila almacena energía. Cuando Jo la conecta al motor, la energía hace que el carrito se mueva.
6-8.q: What does the energy do?

6-8.def: a very small group of atoms joined together
6-8.ex: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
6-8.clip: A molecule of water is made of three atoms. When water heats up, its molecules move faster.
6-8.clipEs: Una molécula de agua está formada por tres átomos. Cuando el agua se calienta, sus moléculas se mueven más rápido.
6-8.q: What happens when water heats up?

6-8.def: the force that pulls objects toward each other
6-8.ex: Gravity keeps the planets in orbit.
6-8.clip: Gravity pulls the apple down from the tree. The moon is also held near Earth by gravity.
6-8.clipEs: La gravedad jala la manzana hacia abajo desde el árbol. La luna también se mantiene cerca de la Tierra por la gravedad.
6-8.q: What holds the moon near Earth?

6-8.def: a comparison of parts, or a statement that two ratios are equal
6-8.ex: The recipe uses a proportion of two cups of rice to four cups of water.
6-8.clip: The recipe uses two cups of rice for every four cups of water. To make more, Ben keeps the same proportion.
6-8.clipEs: La receta usa dos tazas de arroz por cada cuatro tazas de agua. Para hacer más, Ben mantiene la misma proporción.
6-8.q: What does Ben keep the same?

6-8.def: how likely it is that something will happen
6-8.ex: The probability of rain is high.
6-8.clip: There are five red marbles and one blue marble in the bag. The probability of picking a red marble is high.
6-8.clipEs: Hay cinco canicas rojas y una azul en la bolsa. La probabilidad de sacar una canica roja es alta.
6-8.q: Which color is more likely to be picked?

6-8.def: a number found by adding values and dividing by how many there are
6-8.ex: The average score was eighty.
6-8.clip: Three scores are 6, 8, and 10. To find the average, Ana adds them to get 24 and divides by three.
6-8.clipEs: Tres puntajes son 6, 8 y 10. Para hallar el promedio, Ana los suma para obtener 24 y divide entre tres.
6-8.q: What does Ana divide by?

6-8.def: less than zero
6-8.ex: A negative number is less than zero.
6-8.clip: The temperature drops to negative five degrees. Water outside freezes into ice.
6-8.clipEs: La temperatura baja a cinco grados bajo cero. El agua de afuera se congela.
6-8.q: What happens to the water outside?

6-8.def: a pair of numbers that tells the exact place of a point on a grid
6-8.ex: The coordinates of the treasure are (3, 5).
6-8.clip: On the map, the park is at coordinates (4, 2). Hana moves four units right and two units up from the start.
6-8.clipEs: En el mapa, el parque está en las coordenadas (4, 2). Hana se mueve cuatro unidades a la derecha y dos hacia arriba desde el inicio.
6-8.q: How many units up does Hana move?

6-8.def: to find a number that is close to the exact answer
6-8.ex: I estimate the cost before I shop.
6-8.clip: Before shopping, Cora estimates the total. She rounds each price to the nearest dollar and adds them.
6-8.clipEs: Antes de comprar, Cora estima el total. Redondea cada precio al dólar más cercano y los suma.
6-8.q: How does Cora estimate?

6-8.def: a statement that two amounts are not equal
6-8.ex: The inequality x > 3 means x is greater than three.
6-8.clip: The sign says riders must be at least four feet tall. The inequality h ≥ 4 describes who can ride.
6-8.clipEs: El letrero dice que los pasajeros deben medir al menos cuatro pies. La desigualdad h ≥ 4 describe quién puede subir.
6-8.q: Who can ride?
6-8.a: Anyone at least four feet tall

6-8.def: to combine parts so they work together as one
6-8.ex: Authors integrate quotes into their writing.
6-8.clip: Keisha integrates a quote into her essay. She introduces the quote first and then explains what it shows.
6-8.clipEs: Keisha integra una cita en su ensayo. Primero presenta la cita y luego explica lo que muestra.
6-8.q: What does Keisha do after the quote?

6-8.def: using few words to say a lot
6-8.ex: A concise summary is short but complete.
6-8.clip: The teacher asks for a concise summary. Omar cuts extra words and keeps only the key events in two sentences.
6-8.clipEs: La maestra pide un resumen conciso. Omar elimina palabras extra y deja solo los eventos clave en dos oraciones.
6-8.q: How long is Omar's summary?

6-8.def: the writer's attitude shown by word choice
6-8.ex: The tone of the letter is polite.
6-8.clip: The author's tone is hopeful. She uses words like "bright," "chance," and "begin" to show she expects good things.
6-8.clipEs: El tono de la autora es esperanzado. Usa palabras como "bright", "chance" y "begin" para mostrar que espera cosas buenas.
6-8.q: What is the author's tone?

6-8.def: the big message or lesson of a story
6-8.ex: A theme of the story is that courage can be quiet.
6-8.clip: The theme of the novel is that friendship takes effort. The characters repair their bond by listening and saying sorry.
6-8.clipEs: El tema de la novela es que la amistad requiere esfuerzo. Los personajes reparan su vínculo escuchando y pidiendo perdón.
6-8.q: What is the theme of the novel?

6-8.def: when what happens is the opposite of what you expect
6-8.ex: There is irony when a fire station burns down.
6-8.clip: The irony is that the lifeguard cannot swim. Readers expect a lifeguard to be a strong swimmer.
6-8.clipEs: La ironía es que el salvavidas no sabe nadar. Los lectores esperan que un salvavidas sea un buen nadador.
6-8.q: What is ironic about the lifeguard?

6-8.def: an idea that disagrees with your claim
6-8.ex: A strong essay answers a counterclaim.
6-8.clip: Leo argues for a longer lunch. A counterclaim is that classes would end later, so he answers it with a plan to shorten the passing time.
6-8.clipEs: Leo defiende un almuerzo más largo. Un contraargumento es que las clases terminarían más tarde, así que lo responde con un plan para acortar el cambio de clase.
6-8.q: How does Leo answer the counterclaim?

6-8.def: connected to the topic in a useful way
6-8.ex: Choose evidence that is relevant to your claim.
6-8.clip: Nina writes about recycling. A fact about cafeteria trash is relevant, but a fact about soccer is not.
6-8.clipEs: Nina escribe sobre el reciclaje. Un dato sobre la basura de la cafetería es pertinente, pero uno sobre fútbol no lo es.
6-8.q: Which fact is relevant?

6-8.def: to give special importance to something
6-8.ex: The speaker emphasizes the most important word.
6-8.clip: The author emphasizes the danger by repeating the word "storm." Each time, the sentences get shorter and faster.
6-8.clipEs: La autora enfatiza el peligro repitiendo la palabra "storm". Cada vez, las oraciones son más cortas y rápidas.
6-8.q: How does the author emphasize the danger?

6-8.def: the words or situation around something that help explain its meaning
6-8.ex: Use context clues to find a word's meaning.
6-8.clip: Sam does not know the word "scarce." The sentence says water was scarce, so people saved every drop. Sam uses the context to figure it out.
6-8.clipEs: Sam no conoce la palabra "scarce". La oración dice que el agua era escasa, así que la gente ahorraba cada gota. Sam usa el contexto para deducirla.
6-8.q: What does Sam use to figure out the word?

6-8.def: the standards used to judge something
6-8.ex: The criteria for the project are on the rubric.
6-8.clip: The judges use three criteria: the idea, the evidence, and the clarity. Each team reads the criteria before they begin.
6-8.clipEs: Los jueces usan tres criterios: la idea, la evidencia y la claridad. Cada equipo lee los criterios antes de empezar.
6-8.q: How many criteria do the judges use?

6-8.def: to discuss a topic with people who have different views
6-8.ex: The class will debate the new schedule.
6-8.clip: The class will debate whether the school should have uniforms. Each side gets three minutes to share reasons, and then they listen to the other side.
6-8.clipEs: La clase debatirá si la escuela debería tener uniformes. Cada lado tiene tres minutos para dar razones, y luego escuchan al otro lado.
6-8.q: What do both sides do?

6-8.def: a comparison of two amounts, like 3 to 2
6-8.ex: The ratio of boys to girls is three to two.
6-8.clip: In the garden, there are six tomato plants and four pepper plants. The ratio of tomato plants to pepper plants is six to four, or three to two.
6-8.clipEs: En el jardín hay seis plantas de tomate y cuatro de pimiento. La razón de plantas de tomate a plantas de pimiento es seis a cuatro, o tres a dos.
6-8.q: What is the ratio of tomato plants to pepper plants?

6-8.def: a math sentence that says two amounts are equal
6-8.ex: The equation x + 3 = 8 has the solution x = 5.
6-8.clip: Tia writes an equation for the story: x plus three equals eight. She subtracts three from both sides and finds that x is five.
6-8.clipEs: Tia escribe una ecuación para el problema: x más tres es igual a ocho. Resta tres de ambos lados y halla que x es cinco.
6-8.q: What is x?

6-8.def: any living thing
6-8.ex: A bacterium is a tiny organism.
6-8.clip: Under the microscope, the class sees a tiny organism swim across the drop of pond water. It is too small to see with the eyes alone.
6-8.clipEs: Con el microscopio, la clase ve un organismo diminuto nadar por la gota de agua del estanque. Es demasiado pequeño para verse a simple vista.
6-8.q: What do they use to see the organism?

6-8.def: tools and machines people make to solve problems
6-8.ex: Technology can help farmers save water.
6-8.clip: New technology helps farmers. Small sensors in the soil tell them when plants need water, so they do not waste any.
6-8.clipEs: La nueva tecnología ayuda a los agricultores. Pequeños sensores en la tierra les dicen cuándo las plantas necesitan agua, así que no desperdician nada.
6-8.q: What do the sensors tell farmers?

6-8.def: a list of numbers or events in a certain order
6-8.ex: The sequence 2, 4, 6, 8 grows by two each time.
6-8.clip: The sequence starts at three and grows by four each time: 3, 7, 11. The next number is fifteen.
6-8.clipEs: La secuencia empieza en tres y crece de cuatro en cuatro: 3, 7, 11. El siguiente número es quince.
6-8.q: What is the next number?

6-8.def: based on good reasons or facts
6-8.ex: A valid argument uses accurate evidence.
6-8.clip: The reasoning is valid because every step follows from the facts. The conclusion would be weak if the data came from only one test.
6-8.clipEs: El razonamiento es válido porque cada paso se deduce de los datos. La conclusión sería débil si los datos vinieran de una sola prueba.
6-8.q: Why is the reasoning valid?
6-8.a: Every step follows from the facts

6-8.def: to make something less harmful or severe
6-8.ex: Trees mitigate the heat in cities.
6-8.clip: Planting trees along the street can mitigate the heat. Their shade lowers the temperature on the sidewalk by several degrees.
6-8.clipEs: Plantar árboles a lo largo de la calle puede mitigar el calor. Su sombra baja varios grados la temperatura de la acera.
6-8.q: How do trees mitigate the heat?
